summary: JavaScript has no generics or static types. JSDoc comments like @template T and @param {T[]} items describe types for your editor, and a runtime check with typeof is the only thing that stops a wrong type while the program runs.
notes: @template T in a JSDoc comment declares a type variable, like <T> in Java. Node ignores every comment.
TypeScript is a separate language that adds real type checking to JavaScript, with syntax like class Box<T>. Its checker reports new Box<string>(404) as an error before the code runs.
typeof s === "number" checks the actual type of a value while the program runs.
pitfall: Expecting a JSDoc type to stop bad data. Without the typeof check, average([88, "95", 72]) returns 296524 with no error, because 88 + "95" joins the two into the string "8895", then "889572", and / turns that back into a number.
contrast: Java's compiler checks generics, and Python stores hints that tools like mypy check. Plain JavaScript has no type syntax at all, so types live in JSDoc comments or in TypeScript.
